chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Follow-up on names: full name, nickname Reb, sister Anna and Miss Augustine
summary: Second session May 5, 1980: full name Benjamin Franklin Spikes, the nickname Reb from his father, sister Anna May, and Miss Augustine.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: This is May 5, 1980, and this is our second session of the Oral History with Reb Spikes. Reb, I listened to the first part of the interview we did, and I have a few questions I'd like to clear up. First of all, we did not get your full name. We only got Benjamin Spikes. Tell me your full name.
I see. Named after Benjamin Franklin. And I read in one of the articles about you that the reason you're called
Well, I don't know. My father, I guess, just... I guess I was a rebel. I was maybe so mean [laughs] and mischievous that he called me that, and that just stuck with me all these years.
And you said a minute or so ago that as far back as you can remember...
Yes, as far back as I can remember...
...you've been "Reb." Then, on the tape, it was a little difficult to understand...uh, the name of one of your sisters. I got Viola clearly but the other sister's name is...
Anna May, I think it is. I think it was Anna May, but 'course I don't...I see her name--she always signed it "Annie M." so I think it was May.
Okay. This Miss Augustine that taught music from your house. Was Augustine her last name?
Do you remember what her first name was?
She was always just Miss Augustine?
That's all. To me. I think she was German.
